questions.subject: engineering-mathematics
questions.question:
Two independent random variables X and Y are uniformly distributed in the
interval [-1,1]. The probability that max [X,Y] is less than 1/2 is
questions.explanation:
\(-1 \leq x\leq 1 \text{ and } -1 \leq y\leq 1\) is the entire rectangle.The region in which maximum of {x,y} is less than 1/2 is shown below as shaded regioninside this rectangle.

\[\begin{aligned} P\left ( max{x,y} \lt \frac{1}{2} \right )&=\frac{\text{Area of shaded region}}{\text{Area of entire rectangle}} \\ &= \frac{\frac{3}{2} \times \frac{3}{2}}{2 \times 2}=\frac{9}{16} \end{aligned}\]

questions.subject: engineering-mathematics
questions.question: Given \(f(z)=\frac{1}{z+1}-\frac{2}{z+3}\). If C is a counter clockwise path in the z-plane such that |z+1|=1, the value of \(\frac{1}{2 \pi j}\oint_{C}f(z)dz\) is
questions.explanation:
Given:
\[\begin{aligned} f(z)&=\frac{1}{z+1}-\frac{2}{z+3}\\ &=\frac{(Z+3)-2(Z+1)}{(Z+1)(Z+3)}\\ &=\frac{-Z+1}{(Z+1)(Z+3)} \end{aligned}\]
Poles are at -1 and -3 i.e. (-1,0) and (-3,0).
From figure below of |Z+1|=1,
we see that (-1,0) is inside the circle and (-3,0) is outside the circle.

Residue theorem says,
\(\frac{1}{2 \pi j}\oint _Cf(z)dz=\)Residue of those poles which are inside C.
So the required integral \(\frac{1}{2 \pi j}\oint _Cf(z)dz\) is given by the residue of function at poles (-1,0) ( which is inside the circle).
This residue is \(=\frac{-(-1)+1}{(-1+3)}=\frac{2}{2}=1\)

questions.question: With initial condition x(1)=0.5, the solution of the differential equation \(t\frac{dx}{dt}+x=t\), is
questions.explanation:
The given differential equation is \(\frac{tdx}{dt}+x=t\) with initial condition \(x(t)=\frac{1}{2}\) which is same as \(\frac{dx}{dt}+\frac{x}{t}=1\)
Which is a linear differential equation
\(\frac{dx}{dt}+P{x}=Q\)
Where, \(P=\frac{1}{t}\) and Q=1
Integrating factor \(=e^{\int P\;dt}=e^{\int \frac{1}{t}dt}=e^{\log _{e}t}=t\)
Solution is
\[\begin{aligned} x\cdot (IF) &=\int Q\cdot (IF)dt +C\\ x\cdot t&= \int 1\cdot t\cdot dt+C\\ xt&= \frac{t^2}{2}+C\\ x&= \frac{t}{2}+\frac{C}{t}\\ \text{Put } x(1)&=\frac{1}{2} \\ \Rightarrow \; \frac{1}{2}+\frac{C}{1}&=\frac{1}{2} \\ \Rightarrow \; C&=0 \\ \text{So, }x&=\frac{t}{2}\text{ is the solution.} \end{aligned}\]

questions.question: The unilateral Laplace transform of \(f(t)\) is \(\frac{1}{s^{2}+s+1}\). The unilateral Laplace transform of \(tf(t)\) is
questions.explanation: \[\begin{aligned} \text{If }L[f(t)]&=\bar{f}(s)\\ \text{then, }L[t^nf(t)]&=(-1)^n\frac{d^n}{ds^n}\bar{f}(s)\\ &\text{In this problem,}\\ \text{Given, }L[f(t)]&=\frac{1}{s^2+s+1}=\bar{f}(s)\\ &\text{We need,}\\ L[tf(t)]&=(-1)^n\frac{d^1}{ds^1}\bar{f}(s)\\ &=-\frac{d}{ds}\bar{f}(s)\\ &=-\frac{d}{ds}\left [ \frac{1}{s^2+s+1} \right ]\\ &=-\left [ \frac{-1}{(s^2+s+1)^2} \right ] \times (2s+1)\\ &=\frac{2s+1}{(s^2+s+1)^2} \end{aligned}\]

questions.subject: power-systems
questions.question:
The figure shows a two-generator system applying a load of \(P_D\)= 40MW, connected at bus 2.

The fuel cost of generators G1 and G2 are :
\(C_1(P_{G1})\)=10,000 Rs/MWh and \(C_2(P_{G2})\)=12,500 Rs/MWh and the loss in the line is \(P_{loass(pu)}=0.5P_{G1(pu)}^2\), where the loss coefficient is specified in pu on a 100 MVA base. The most economic power generation schedule in MW is
questions.explanation:
From cordination equation
\[\begin{aligned} \frac{dF_n}{dP_{Gn}}\cdot \frac{1}{1-\frac{\partial P_L}{\partial P_{Gn}}}&=\lambda \\ \text{Given: }P_L&=0.5P_{G1}^2\\ \frac{\partial P_L}{\partial P_{G1}}=P_{G1} \text{ and } \frac{\partial P_L}{\partial P_{G2}}&= 0\\ \Rightarrow \; \frac{dF_{1}}{dP_{G1}}\frac{1}{1-P_{G1}}&=\frac{dF_2}{dP_{G2}}\frac{1}{1-0}\\ \Rightarrow \; 10000 \times \frac{1}{1-P_{G1}}&=12500\\ 1-P_{G1}=\frac{100}{125}&=\frac{4}{5}\\ P_{G1}&=\frac{1}{5}p.u.\\ \end{aligned}\]
as the base value is 100 MVA
\[\begin{aligned} P_{G1}&=\frac{1}{5} \times 100=20MW\\ \Rightarrow \; P_L&=0.5P_{G1}^2\\ &=0.5\left ( \frac{1}{5} \right )^2=0.02p.u.\\ \Rightarrow \; P_L&=0.02 \times 100=2MW\\ P_D&=P_{G1}+P_{G2}-P_L\\ 40&=20+P_{G2}-2\\ \Rightarrow \;\;P_{G2}&=22 MV \end{aligned}\]

questions.subject: engineering-mathematics
questions.question:
Given that
\[A=\begin{bmatrix} -5 &-3 \\ 2&0 \end{bmatrix} \; and \; I=\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0\\ 0&1 \end{bmatrix}\], the value of \(A^{3}\) is
questions.explanation:
\[A=\begin{bmatrix} -5 & -3\\ 2& 0 \end{bmatrix}\] and \[I=\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0\\ 0& 1 \end{bmatrix}\]
Characteristic equation of A is
\[\begin{bmatrix} -5-\lambda & -3\\ 2& 0-\lambda \end{bmatrix}=0\]
\((-5-\lambda )(-\lambda )+6=0\)
\(\Rightarrow \;\; \lambda ^2+5\lambda +6=0\)
\(\text{So, } A^2+5A+6I=0\)
(by Cayley Hamilton theorem)
\(\Rightarrow \;\; A^2=-5A-6I\)
Multiplying by A on both sides, we have,
\(A^3=-5A^2-6A\)
\(\Rightarrow \;\; A^3=-5(-5A-6I)-6A=19A+30I\)

questions.subject: engineering-mathematics
questions.question: The maximum value of \(f(x)=x^{3}-9x^{2}+24x+5\) in the interval [1,6] is
questions.explanation:
We need absolute maximum of
\(f(x)=x^3-9x^2+24x+5\) in the interval of [1,6]
First find local maximum if any by putting f'(x)=0.
\[\begin{aligned} f'(x) &=3x^2-18x+24=0 \\ x^2-6x+8&=0 \\ x&=2,4 \\ \text{Now } f''(x) &=6x-18 \\ f''(2)&=12-18=-6 \lt 0 \\ \text{(So } x&=2 \text{ is a point of local maximum)} \\ f''(4)&=24-18=+6 \gt 0 \\ \text{(So } x&=4 \text{ is a point of local minimum)} \\ \end{aligned}\]
Now tabulate the value of f at end point of interval and at local maximum point, to find absolute maximum in given range, as shown below
\[\begin{matrix} x& f(x)\\ 1& 21\\ 2 & 25\\ 6& 41 \end{matrix}\]
Clearly the absolute maxima is at x=6 and absolute maximum value is 41.

questions.question: Let y[n] denote the convolution of h[n] and g[n], where h[n]=\((1/2)^{n}\)u[n] and g[n] is a causal sequence. If y[0]=1 and y[1]=1/2, then g[1] equals
questions.explanation:

Therefore, g[n] will be zero for \(n \lt 0\)
\[\begin{aligned} y[n]&=\sum_{k=-\infty }^{\infty }g[k]h[n-k]\\ h[n]&=\left ( \frac{1}{2} \right )^n u[n]\\ h[n]&=\left\{\begin{matrix} \left ( \frac{1}{2} \right )^n \; ;& n\geq 0\\ 0& n \lt 0 \end{matrix}\right.\\ h[0]&=0, h[1]=\frac{1}{2}, h[2]=\frac{1}{4}\\ y[0]&=g[0] h[0]+g[1]h[-1]+...\\ 1&=g[0] \times 1+0+0+...\\ g[0]&=1\\ y[1]&=g[0]h[1]+g[1]h[0]+g[2]h[-1]+...\\ \frac{1}{2}&=1\cdot \frac{1}{2}+g[1]\cdot 1+0\\ \Rightarrow \;g[1]&=0 \end{aligned}\]

bus through a transmission line of reactance 0.5 pu. The generator no-load voltage

Critical clearing angle
\[\begin{aligned} \delta _{cr}&=\cos ^{-1}[(\pi-2\delta _0) \sin \delta _0 -\cos \delta _0]\\ &=\cos ^{-1}\left [ \left ( \pi-\frac{\pi}{3} \right ) \times \frac{1}{2} -\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right ]\\ &= \cos ^{-1} (0.18)=79.56^{\circ} \end{aligned}\]

questions.subject: engineering-mathematics
questions.question:
A fair coin is tossed till a head appears for the first time. The probability that the
number of required tosses is odd, is
questions.explanation:
P(number of tosses is odd) = P(number of tosses is 1,3,5,7?)
P(no. of toss is 1) = P(Head in first toss)=1/2
P(no. of toss is 3) = P( tail in first toss , tail in second toss and head in third toss) \(=\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{2} =\frac{1}{8}\)
P(no. of toss id 5) =P(T, T, T, T, H) \(=\left (\frac{1}{2} \right ) ^5=\frac{1}{32}\)
So P(no. of tosses is odd) \(=\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{8}+\frac{1}{32}+...\)
Sum of infinite geometric series with \(a=\frac{1}{2}\) and \(r=\frac{1}{4}\)
\(=\frac{\frac{1}{2}}{1-\frac{1}{4}}=\frac{\frac{1}{2}}{\frac{3}{4}}=\frac{2}{3}\)

questions.subject: electromagnetic-fields
questions.question: The direction of vector A is radially outward from the origin, with \(|A|=kr^{n}\), where \(r^{2}=x^{2}+y^{2}+z^{2}\) and k is a constant. The value of n for which \(\bigtriangledown \cdot A= 0\) is
questions.explanation: \[\begin{aligned} \vec{A} &=kr^n\hat{i}_r \\ \triangledown \cdot \vec{A} &= \frac{1}{r^2}\frac{\partial }{\partial r}(r^2 k r^n)\\ &=\frac{1}{r^2}\frac{\partial }{\partial r}( k r^{n+2}) \\ &= (n+2)k\frac{r^{n+1}}{r^2}\\ &= (n+2)kr^{n-1}\\ \text{For}\;\; \triangledown \cdot \vec{A} &= 0\\ n+2 &=0\\ \Rightarrow \;\; n=-2 \end{aligned}\]

questions.subject: signals-and-systems
questions.question:
Consider the differential equation
\(\frac{d^{2}y(t)}{dt^{2}}+2\frac{dy(t)}{dt}+y(t)=\delta (t)\) with \(y(t)|_{t=0^{-}}=-2\) and \(\frac{dy}{dt}|_{t=0^{-}}=0\)
The numerical value of \(\frac{dy}{dt}|_{t=0^{+}}\), is
questions.explanation: \[\begin{aligned} &\frac{d^2y(t)}{dt^2}+2\frac{dy(t)}{dt}+y(t)=\delta (t)\\ &\Rightarrow \; s^2y(s)-sy(0)-y'(0)+2[sy(s)-y(0)]\\&+y(s)=1\\ &\Rightarrow \; y(s)[s^22s+1]-(s \times -2)-y(0)\\&-(2 \times -2)=1\\ &\Rightarrow \; y(s)[s^2+2a+1]=-2s-3\\ &\Rightarrow \;y(s)=\frac{-2s-3}{s^2+2s+1}=\frac{-2}{s+1}-\frac{1}{(s+1)^2}\\ &\Rightarrow \; y(t)=-2e^{-t}-te^{-t}\\ &\frac{dy(t)}{dt}=2e^{-t}-(-te^{-t}+e^{-t})\\ &\frac{dy(t)}{dt}=e^{-t}+te^{-t}\\ &\frac{dy(t)}{dt}|_{t=0^+}=1+0=1 \end{aligned}\]

\[y=(1 \;\;0\;\; 0)\begin{pmatrix} x_{1}\\ x_{2}\\ x_{3} \end{pmatrix}\]
where y is the output and u is the input. The system is controllable for
questions.explanation:
\[A= egin{bmatrix} 0 &a_1 &0 \ 0 & 0& a_2\ a_3& 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix},\] \[B= egin{bmatrix} 0\ 0\ 1 \end{bmatrix},\] \[C= egin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix}^T\]
For stable system to be controllable, the metric \(Q_c\) must be non singular.

\(|Q_c|=-a_1a_2^2\)
For \(Q_c\) to be nonsingular
\(|Q_c| eq 0\)

questions.subject: signals-and-systems
questions.question: The Fourier transform of a signal h(t) is \(H(j \omega)=(2\cos\omega)(\sin 2 \omega)/\omega\). The value of h(0) is
questions.explanation: \[\begin{aligned} H(j\omega )&=\cos \omega \cdot \frac{2 \sin 2\omega }{\omega }\\ &=\frac{e^{j\omega}+e^{-j\omega}}{2}\cdot \frac{2 \sin 2\omega }{\omega }\\ &=\frac{1}{2}\left [ e^{j\omega}\left ( \frac{2 \sin 2\omega }{\omega } \right )+e^{-j\omega}\left ( \frac{2 \sin 2\omega }{\omega } \right ) \right ]\\ \text{Let, }X(\omega )&=\frac{2 \sin 2\omega }{\omega } \\ \text{Then, }x(t)&=\left\{\begin{matrix} 1 & -2 \lt t \lt 2\\ 0 & \text{ otherwise} \end{matrix}\right. \\ &\text{By time shifting property}\\ h(t)&=\frac{1}{2}(x(t+1)+x(t-1))\\ \therefore \; h(0)&=\frac{1}{2}[x(1)+x(-1)]=\frac{1}{2}[1+1]=1 \end{aligned}\]

questions.subject: signals-and-systems
questions.question: The input x(t) and output y(t) of a system are related as \(y(t)=\int^{t}_{-\infty }x(\tau ) cos (3\tau )d\tau\). The system is
questions.explanation:
\[\begin{aligned} y&=\int_{-\infty }^{t}x{\tau } \cos (3\tau )d\tau \\ y(t-t_0)&=\int_{-\infty }^{t-t_0}x{\tau } \cos (3\tau )d\tau\\ y(t) & \text{ for input }x(t-t_0) \text{ is}\\ y'(t)&=\int_{-\infty }^{t}x{\tau -t_0} \cos (3\tau )d\tau\\ y'(t)&=\int_{-\infty }^{t-t_0}x{\tau} \cos 3(\tau +t_0 )d\tau\\ y'(t) &\neq y(t-t_0) \end{aligned}\]
So, system is not time invariant for input \(x{\tau } =\cos (3\tau )\) bounded input
\(y(t)=\int_{-\infty }^{t} \cos ^2 (3\tau )d\tau \rightarrow \infty \; as \; t \rightarrow \infty\)
So, for bounded input, output is not bounded therefore system is not stable.

questions.explanation: \[\begin{aligned} when, \;\; R_{s_1}&=20k\Omega ,\;\; v=440V\\ V&=\frac{440}{R_m}\times 20+440\;\;...(i)\\ when, \;\; R_{s_2}&=80k\Omega ,\;\; v=352V \\ V&=\frac{352}{R_m}\times 80+352\;\;...(ii) \\ \Rightarrow \; R_m &= \frac{352 \times 80- 440 \times 20}{88}\\ R_m &= 220 k\Omega ,\;V=480V\\ when, \;\;R_{s_3} &=40k\Omega \text{and} V=480V \\ 480 &=\frac{v}{R_m} \times 40+v \\ 480 &= \frac{13}{11}v \\ \Rightarrow \; v &= 406.15 V \end{aligned}\]

questions.subject: electrical-machines
questions.question:
The locked rotor current in a 3-phase, star connected 15 kW, 4 pole, 230 V, 50 Hz
induction motor at rated conditions is 50 A. Neglecting losses and magnetizing
current, the approximate locked rotor line current drawn when the motor is
connected to a 236 V, 57 Hz supply is
questions.explanation:
At standstill, the rotor current is
\(I_2=\frac{E_2}{\sqrt{R^2+X^2}}\)
As losses are zero
\[\begin{aligned} \Rightarrow \;\;I_2 &=\frac{E_2}{X}=\frac{E_2}{j\omega L} \\ \therefore \;\; \frac{I_2}{I'_2} &=\frac{E_2}{E'_2} \times \frac{\omega '}{\omega } \\ \Rightarrow \;\; I'_2 &=\frac{236 \times 50}{230 \times 57} \times 50=45A \end{aligned}\]

questions.question:
A single phase 10 kVA, 50 Hz transformer with 1 kV primary winding draws
0.5 A and 55W, at rated voltage and frequency, on no load. A second transformer
has a core with all its linear dimensions \(\sqrt{2}\) times the corresponding dimensions
of the first transformer. The core material and lamination thickness are the same
in both transformer. The primary winding of both the transformers have the save
number of turns. If a rate voltage of 2 kV at 50 Hz is applied to the primary of
the second transformer, then the no load current and power, respectively, are
questions.explanation:
We know, \(E=\sqrt{2} \pi N f \phi _m\),
As N and f are constant,
\[\begin{aligned} \frac{E_1}{E_2} &=\frac{\phi _{m1}}{\phi _{m2}}=\frac{1}{2} \\ \phi _{m2}&=2\phi _{m1} \\ \text{and also,}\;\; \phi _m &= \frac{\mu NiA}{d}\\ \Rightarrow \; &= \\ \frac{\phi _{m1}}{\phi _{m2}} &=\frac{i_{e1} A_1d_2}{i_{e2}A_2d_1} \\ &= \frac{\sqrt{2}i_{e1}}{2i_{e2}}=\frac{1}{2}\\ \Rightarrow \;\;i_{e2}&=\sqrt{2} i_{e1} \\ \Rightarrow \;\;i_{e2} &= \sqrt{2} \frac{1}{2}=0.7A\\ \text{Core loss}&\propto \text{Volume of core,} \\ \therefore \;\;\;P_{c2} &=\frac{V_2}{V_1} P_{c1}\\ &=2\sqrt{2} \times 55=155.6W \end{aligned}\]

questions.subject: control-systems
questions.question:
The transfer function of a compensator is given as
\(G_c(s)=\frac{s+a}{s+b}\)
\(G_c(s)\) is a lead compensator if
questions.explanation:
\(G_c(s)=\frac{s+a}{s+b}\)
\(G_c(j\omega )=\frac{j\omega +a}{j\omega +b}\)
\(\angle G_c(j\omega )=tan^{-1}\frac{\omega }{a}-tan^{-1}\frac{\omega }{b}\)
\(\;\;\;= tan^{-1}\left ( \frac{\frac{\omega }{a}-\frac{\omega }{b}}{1+\frac{\omega ^2 }{ab}} \right )\)
For \(G_c(s)\) to be a lead compensator
\(\angle G_c(j\omega ) \gt 0\)
\(\frac{\omega }{a} \gt \frac{\omega }{b}\)
\(\Rightarrow b \gt a\)
Option (A) Satisfies the above equation.
